answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a glacier as the anchor of the cost.
